paras: The lynching of Sharp McNut took place at Star City, Arkansas, around midnight on January 18, 1881, when an armed, masked mob of about one hundred men took him from the town jail and shot him to death. McNut was being held on a charge of murdering Dr. E. C. G. Anderson. Papers in Louisiana and Tennessee carried the news; neither states his race.
McNut was a prisoner in the Star City jail, charged with the murder of Dr. E. C. G. Anderson.

According to a letter from Judge C. W. Priddy at Star City, the mob entered the town at twelve o'clock on the night of the 18th, captured the jailor and put him under arrest. Its members then forced the jail doors, took McNut out and carried him to the town's outskirts, where they killed him. His body was found there the next morning "riddled with bullets." Priddy wrote that the jailor "found himself overpowered and could do nothing to prevent the acts of the crowd."
The people of Star City were reported to be "much excited over the affair." No report of an inquest, of arrests of mob members or of any official inquiry appears in the coverage.

The news traveled from Priddy's letter to Col. Met L. Jones, then to Major Newman, editor of the Pine Bluff Press, who sent it out in a Pine Bluff dispatch dated January 19. The Louisiana Capitolian of Baton Rouge printed it on January 22 under the headline "A Murderer Lynched at Star City," calling McNut a murderer although the dispatch itself said only that he was "charged with" the crime. On January 26 the Memphis Daily Appeal condensed the story to a single sentence in its "Arkansas Atoms" column, spelling the name "Sharpe McNeil" and dating the lynching to "last Tuesday night"; the Pine Bluff version, earlier and fuller, gave "Sharp McNut."

Both papers reported the mob's acts without comment, and neither mentioned the race of the prisoner, the mob or the doctor. The two items agree in detail and appear to rest on the same Arkansas report.

bases: An armed, masked mob of about one hundred men forced the Star City jail, took out a man charged with murder and shot him to death (A1, A2).

A masked mob of a hundred men overpowered the jailor, took the prisoner from jail and killed him, with no lawful authority, because he was charged with the murder of Dr. E. C. G. Anderson (A1, A2). Neither paper states the victim's race.

Both items agree on the core event, but A1 traces to a single letter from Judge C. W. Priddy relayed through the Pine Bluff Press, and the shorter A2 item (same mob size, same doctor's initials) appears to derive from the same Arkansas report rather than an independent one (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Memphis Appeal state-news item
accounts.gist: 'Sharpe McNeil', charged with Anderson's murder, was taken from the Star City jail on Tuesday night by an armed masked mob of a hundred and riddled with bullets.

framing.detail: The Baton Rouge paper headlined the dispatch 'A Murderer Lynched at Star City', calling the prisoner a murderer though the text says only that he was 'charged with' the killing; the dispatch otherwise reports the mob's acts without comment.
The Memphis Daily Appeal gave the lynching one sentence among Arkansas briefs on diphtheria, frozen peach trees and a gold-headed cane, without comment.
